the results of these studies have failed to substantiate the claims of superiority of the new agents.
the hypotensive effect of the drugs tested was not of sufficient magnitude to warrant the use of these drugs as the primary hypotensive agent in the treatment of human hypertension.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of hydrallazine, hexamethonium, and tetraethylamnonium salts in hypertension is not warranted.
the use of hydrallazine in hypertension is not justified.
the hypotensive action of hydrallazine salts in man is comparable to that obtained with the hexamethonium and dibenzyline salts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a very good understanding of how to use hydrallazine to treat hypertension in humans.
the use of hydrallazine, hexamethonium, tetraethylammonoim chloride and Dibenxyline salts in the treatment of hypertension is of limited value and is not to be recommended.
the use of hydrallazine in combination with hexamethonium or other ganglionic blocking agents does not appear to be a rational approach in the treatment of human hypertension.
